sections.h2: Is a quick sale right for your Kennesaw house?
sections.html:
A quick sale fits Kennesaw owners who face repairs, an estate to settle or a payment problem, while a full listing suits those with time and a tidy house. The 2025 estimate for the city is 37,970 residents, against 33,036 counted in 2020. That growth keeps buyers active, though it also puts many listings near the university and along Cobb Parkway.

Speed matters most when a house needs work, sits empty or carries a loan you cannot keep paying. In those cases weigh the closing date and repair bill against the price. Write down the net under each route before choosing one.

Kennesaw sits in a county with its own tax office, so deeds and bills involve both Cobb County and the city.

Kennesaw covers about 9.5 square miles in northwest Cobb County. U.S. 41 and State Route 3 run through town as Cobb Parkway, and Interstate 75 clips the northeast corner with exits 269, 271 and 273. Downtown Atlanta is about 27 miles southeast. Houses a short drive from the I-75 exits are the easiest for a buyer to place on a map.

For 2020 to 2024 there are 13,554 households here, 64.6 percent of them owner occupied. Median home value is $335,400 and median gross rent is $1,845. Renting is an option if you inherit and prefer not to sell right away.

  • Median household income: $83,356 (in 2024 dollars)
  • Mean commute: 28.6 minutes

Kennesaw State University is the biggest anchor, so ask a local agent how much nearby demand ties back to the campus. The Southern Museum of Civil War and Locomotive History downtown and the Kennesaw Mountain battlefield park, with about 18 miles of trails, draw visitors all year. The Big Shanty Festival each April brings crowds downtown.

Mentioning the trails and the downtown depot in a listing gives walkable-history buyers a reason to look.

Humid summers wear on roofs, gutters, crawl spaces and exterior paint, so a buyer's inspector will start with drainage, moisture and the age of the HVAC system. Selling as is, expect those items to set the price. Listing instead, a modest round of fixes to flashing, grading and mechanicals often costs less than the discount requested after inspection.

sections.h2: Who bills property tax and when it is due
sections.html:
Kennesaw owners get two tax bills. Cobb County collects for itself and the school district, and the city runs a separate city bill. The county values property at 40 percent of market value. City bills are mailed October 1 and carry a December 1 due date.

The city's tax covers the full year with no proration, so sharing the bill with a buyer is a contract term. Before signing, ask your closing attorney how each of the two bills will show on the settlement statement.

Kennesaw tax bills and who handles them
Bill or stepOfficeTiming or rule
County and school taxCobb Tax CommissionerBills go out in August with an October due date
City of Kennesaw taxCity Finance DepartmentMailed October 1, due December 1 each year
Value and appealsCobb Board of Tax Assessors45 days after the notice date
Senior city exemptionCity Finance DepartmentOwner 65 or older by January 1, apply by April 1

Interest begins the morning after the due date. The city then layers on a 5 percent penalty at 120 days and a further 5 percent every 120 days after that, stopping at 20 percent of principal. It also runs an annual tax sale on the first Tuesday in November at City Hall, starting at 9:00 AM, advertised in the Marietta Daily Journal four weeks beforehand.

Pay off any open city or county balance before you take an offer. Title work will find it, and the payoff would otherwise be taken from what you receive.

sections.h2: Selling a house that ran as an Airbnb
sections.html:
It can be sold, though the rental permission may stay behind. The city's short-term rental ordinance (Chapter 22, Article XIII) covers any dwelling let for fewer than 30 consecutive days and calls for both a city business license and a Short-Term Rental Certificate, which expires every December 31. The application fee is $250.

A house operating before January 1, 2025 could register as nonconforming, but that status ends automatically when ownership changes. A new owner who wants nightly guests must meet the current rules: the 8 percent hotel and motel excise tax, the two-property maximum and the 250-foot distance requirement that nonconforming rentals skip. Explain this to buyers early. The Business License Office is at 3080 Moon Station Road.

Open permits cause the most trouble, so ask the city's building and inspections staff whether any permit on the house was left unclosed. Unfinished work from a past owner can stall a buyer with a loan even when a cash buyer would take it as is. Cobb County Fire covers the city, while Kennesaw keeps its own police department and 9-1-1 center at City Hall.

  • Collect permit records and receipts for roof, HVAC and electrical jobs.
  • Confirm no city or county tax balance is outstanding.
  • For a former rental, ask the Business License Office which registrations are still active.

Georgia's transfer tax is $1 for the first $1,000 or fractional part of $1,000 and 10 cents for each additional $100 or fractional part of $100. It is paid before the deed is recorded.

sections.h2: Steps for a quick Kennesaw sale
sections.html:
Whichever buyer you choose, the order of work is similar. First, collect the deed, any estate papers and your loan payoff figure. Second, check the city and county tax balances, because two bills means two places a balance can hide. Third, ask the city about open permits and, for a former rental, about the business license and certificate. Fourth, get written offers and compare the net under each one.

A cash buyer can often close faster because there is no lender to satisfy. A listed sale can bring a higher price, but it adds showings, an inspection and a loan approval. If you have a deadline, such as a foreclosure notice or an estate date, tell every buyer up front so they can say honestly whether they can meet it.

Keep copies of every offer, and do not sign anything until you have read the closing costs and the date the buyer must close by.

faqs.q: How soon could a cash sale close in Kennesaw?
faqs.a: Timing rests on the title search and the buyer, but a cash deal skips underwriting and the lender's appraisal, usually the slowest steps. Leave room for title work and for the transfer tax filing with the Clerk of Superior Court.

faqs.q: Do Cobb and Kennesaw send separate tax bills?
faqs.a: Yes. Cobb bills county and school taxes, and the city mails its own bill October 1 with a December 1 due date. Because the city does not prorate, the split with a buyer is set in your contract.

faqs.q: Is it worth appealing a Cobb assessment before a sale?
faqs.a: Only if the value looks high and the window is open. Owners get 45 days from the date printed on the Notice of Assessment.

faqs.q: Will my homestead exemption follow the house to a buyer?
faqs.a: No. The exemption depends on you owning and living in the home on January 1. Kennesaw also offers its own city exemption for owners 65 and older, applied for by April 1.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Kennesaw house that needs a new roof?
faqs.a: Yes, as is. Expect the offer to reflect the repair cost, and keep permit records on hand so the buyer's inspection and title review go smoothly.
